gaps: The capture contains more than one program (the tail of a psychology course sequence, the complete BS in Social Science, and a partial BS in Sustainable Value Chain). This ledger covers the BS in Social Science, the only program captured in full. The Sustainable Value Chain listing is cut off after its required major core courses; its major electives, capstone and 42-credit business core are not itemized in the capture.

The program-specific elective credit amount is not printed; the program table gives only 'Remaining General Education and Elective Courses 87'. The 49 elective credits were calculated as 120 total − 33 major − 41 general education + 3. The +3 assumes STAT 200 is applied to the general education mathematics requirement. The result matches the upper bound of the printed 'Electives 1–49' range.

STAT 200 (related requirement) 'may be applied to general education requirements' and appears in the sequencing table as fulfilling 'Related and general education/mathematics'. The ledger lists both STAT 200 and the 3-credit Mathematics block, so 3 credits overlap; the listed items sum to 123 against the 120 total.

Residency rules are stated only at the degree level and are not tied to specific courses: at least 30 credits (normally the final 30) at UMGC; half of the major credits at UMGC; at least 15 upper-level credits (300–499) at UMGC. Because none of these is tied to a course, no individual requirement is marked institutionalOnly.
At least half of the major credits must be earned through graded coursework. A minimum grade of C is required for major courses, and a minimum 2.0 GPA overall.

The capture does not specify which upper-level ANTH/BEHS/GERO/PSYC/SOCY courses are allowed beyond the recommended focus lists, and does not specify a required course distribution within the 12 major elective credits.

transferMaxCredits.basis: 120 degree credits minus the 90-credit transfer ceiling. The school also requires 15 upper-level credits at the school; 21 upper-level credits in this program (named courses and upper-level-only choices) have no outside option, so the plan always meets it.

alternativeMaxCredits.basis: UMGC counts ACE- and NCCRS-evaluated noncollegiate courses as an external source of credit, limited by the combined maximum from all external sources (45 associate, 90 bachelor’s). No separate ceiling for ACE/NCCRS credit is published.

upperLevelMinimum.basis: UMGC’s bachelor’s degree requirements set no degree-wide upper-level minimum. Their only upper-level rule is 15 upper-level credits (courses numbered 300 to 499) completed at UMGC. This plan’s named upper-level courses with no outside option total 6 of 15 credits, so meeting the rule depends on the student’s choices.
